sections.h2: A journal that follows the Moon
p: Every month the Moon moves from new to full and back again. Many people use this rhythm for journaling: at the new moon they write down an intention, at the full moon they look back and note what they are grateful for.

We calculate the exact moment of every new and full moon with the Swiss Ephemeris and find the house of your birth chart where it falls. Each house has its own theme, so your questions change from month to month instead of repeating the same list.

sections.h2: What this is and what it is not
p: These are questions for reflection, not predictions. We do not tell you what will happen; we offer a rhythm, a few questions and an affirmation, and the answers are yours.
Your answers are saved in your journal so you can find them on any device. We also keep your email and birth data for the letters. You can delete everything at any time with one click.

faq.q: When is the next new moon?
faq.a: The table on this page lists every new and full moon until the end of 2027 with the exact time, and the next one is highlighted.

faq.q: Do I need my birth time?
faq.a: No. Without a birth time we count the houses from your Sun sign. With your birth time and place we count them from your rising sign, which is more personal.

faq.q: What should I write at the new moon?
faq.a: One intention in the present tense and one small step for the coming days. Your personal questions depend on the house where the new moon falls in your chart.

faq.q: What should I write at the full moon?
faq.a: Look back over the last two weeks and name three things you are grateful for. Your letter adds two questions for the house of the full moon.
Yes. The calculator and the letters are free, and every letter has a link to unsubscribe.

plans.title: Two ways to stay close to your own rhythm
plans.lead: The sky is not here to tell you what will happen. It can give you a moment to notice what is already asking for your attention — once at each new and full moon, or as a deeper story unfolding across the whole month.
plans.freeIntro: Twice a month, a short letter meets you at a natural turning point. It translates the new or full moon through your own birth chart and gives you a quiet place to hear yourself more clearly.

freeItems.title: Your sky, in human language
freeItems.text: See which area of life this moon touches and why it may feel more alive now — without jargon or fixed predictions.

freeItems.title: Questions that open something
freeItems.text: Three carefully chosen prompts help you name what you want, what has shifted and what you are ready to carry forward.

freeItems.title: A journal that remembers
freeItems.text: Your answers stay together in a private journal, so a passing feeling can become a pattern you recognise over time.

plans.freeClosing: Free, twice a month. A few thoughtful minutes that belong only to you.
plans.paidIntro: Personal Month gives you the wider view. Instead of meeting the month as a blur of dates, you see its emotional rhythm: the periods that may stir something, the questions worth staying with and the thread connecting it all.

paidItems.title: Your meaningful dates
paidItems.text: A personal calendar of the month's strongest transits, translated into situations you may recognise in work, relationships, home and your inner life.

paidItems.title: Guidance you can actually use
paidItems.text: Each period comes with a focused reflection — not an instruction — so you can make your own choice with more awareness.

paidItems.title: Patterns only time can reveal
paidItems.text: At the end of the month, your entries are reflected back beside the sky of those days, revealing recurring needs, tensions and desires.

paidItems.title: Your year as a story
paidItems.text: On your birthday, those months become a private yearbook: not a list of predictions, but a portrait of how you changed.

plans.paidClosing: For anyone who wants not only to know what is happening in the sky, but to understand what it is opening in their life.
plans.exampleNote: Example for a fictional person born on 17 May 1990. Your own month is calculated from your birth data.

calendar.what: Venus meets your Sun — visibility and self-worth
calendar.text: Compliments may land more deeply this week, or you may notice the moments when you play yourself down. Pay attention to the clothes, people and choices that make you feel more like yourself — not simply more acceptable.
calendar.question: Where are you ready to stop asking for permission to enjoy being yourself?

calendar.what: Mars activates your 4th house — home and belonging
calendar.text: You may feel an urge to clear a corner, address a tension at home or ask for more room of your own. Rather than changing everything, notice the one place — or relationship — that no longer lets you exhale.
calendar.question: If your home could support the person you are becoming, what would you change first, and why?

calendar.what: Full Moon in your 10th house — work and recognition
calendar.text: A result, deadline or conversation may make your progress visible. Before rushing to the next goal, notice what you have built — and whether the version of success you are chasing still feels like yours.
calendar.question: What are you proud to claim as your own, and whose approval are you ready to stop measuring it by?

plans.reviewTitle: Your month in your own words
review: Across seven November entries, three words keep returning: “rest”, “sister” and “project”. Your private life and visible work seem to be asking for attention at the same time.

Near the full moon in your 10th house you wrote: “I want my work to be seen, but not at the cost of coming home depleted.” The same tension appeared in August, when Jupiter crossed the top of your chart.
Carry into December: what would visible success look like if it also left room for your real life?
